title_original: Hoor Al Qasimi Appointed Curator of Venice Art Biennale 2028

blocks.text: The Venice Biennale has announced the appointment of Hoor Al Qasimi as curator of its 62nd International Art Exhibition, due to take place from 9 April to 26 November 2028.

Al Qasimi, who is President and Director of the Sharjah Art Foundation, which she founded in 2009, has also been the Director of the Sharjah Biennial since 2003. A recipient of the insignia of Officier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres, she is currently serving as the 2025–2026 Ambassador Extraordinary for Arab Culture by ALECSO, further cementing her role in fostering cultural and artistic dialogue both in the UAE, the wider region and further afield.

Commenting on her appointment, Al Qasimi shared: “The International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia has been an important platform for many of us around the world. I first visited the 50th edition in 2003 having recently stepped into my curatorial role at Sharjah Biennial. For me, La Biennale continues to be a critical space to engage with the work of influential artists and curators. I am honoured to have been invited to curate this exhibition and grateful to President, Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, and the board for their confidence and trust. I look forward to working with the team of La Biennale and welcoming audiences to the 62nd edition.”

Recognised internationally as a leading figure in contemporary art, she has extensive experience curating major solo and group exhibitions, which include the travelling retrospective of Hassan Sharif in 2017-18 and shows dedicated to the practices of Jorge Tacla, Leda Catunda, Bouchra Khalili, Emily Karaka, William Kentridge, Monir Shahroudy Farmanfarmaian, Rasheed Araeen, Simone Fattal, Farideh Lashai and Yayoi Kusama.

As curator, Al Qasimi has also led major art events across the globe, among them the Lahore Biennial in 2020, most recently serving as Artistic Director for the 6th Aichi Triennale in 2025 and the 25th Biennale of Sydney earlier this year. She presides over numerous cultural organisations, including the International Biennial Association, the Sharjah Museums Authority, The Africa Institute, Sharjah, the Sharjah Architecture Triennale, Sharjah’s Global Studies University, the Sharjah Creative Quarter and the University of the Arts Sharjah.
